passage: Imrana came to Usha's veranda at dusk with mud on her shoes. "I am sorry," she said. "I promised to help you with the goat pen, but my father needed me at the well, and I could not send word." Usha crossed her arms. She had waited by the pen all afternoon. But Imrana's voice was steady and she looked Usha in the eye as she spoke. "All right. I forgive you. Next time, ask someone to tell me." Usha noticed that she would not lend Imrana her best pencil this week. "But if you forget again, I will tell you straight." Imrana nodded and picked up the bucket.

qa.q: Why could Imrana not help Usha with the goat pen?
qa.a: Her father needed her at the well and she could not send word.

qa.q: What might Usha still be worried about after forgiving Imrana?
qa.a: She may worry it could happen again, so she stays careful for a while, as when she would not lend Imrana her best pencil that week.

qa.q: What worked in how Usha handled the broken promise?
qa.a: She forgave Imrana, told her what to do next time, and said she would speak plainly if Imrana forgot again.

qa.q: How might Imrana have felt when Usha crossed her arms?
qa.a: Imrana probably felt nervous and guilty, and showed it by apologising directly and looking Usha in the eye.

grounding: A child forgives a friend who apologises and explains, stays a little careful, and says she will speak up if it keeps happening.
